authority: catalog/vocabulary.json is the single source for these closed value sets. A schema, checker, or reference page that uses one of these sets copies its values from here rather than re-typing them, and a spec compares the copy with this file.

decision.status.description: Where a decision record stands in its own review lifecycle.

values.meaning: Written and offered for a verdict; not yet in force.
Sent back to the proposer for revision; not a rejection.
In force; binding on work that touches the paths it covers.
Refused; the choice it proposed is not taken.
Deliberately not settled yet, with the reason recorded.
Replaced by a later accepted record that points back to it.

decision.stage.description: How far an accepted decision has travelled from words into observed behavior.

values.meaning: Accepted but nothing has been built against it yet.
The change the decision calls for exists in the tree.
A signal observed this time confirms the implementation.

decision.class.description: What kind of choice the record carries, which sets who may settle it.

values.meaning: Direction, portfolio, or ownership of a body of work.
An interface, schema, protocol, or release boundary others build on.
What is built, for whom, and what it promises.
A local, reversible choice inside one team's own scope.

decision.reversibility.description: What it would cost to undo the decision once it is acted on.

values.meaning: Undone at negligible cost; decide fast and revisit.
Undone, but only by paying real migration or rework cost.
Cannot be undone; requires a human verdict before acting.

work-item.next.description: The single next move a work item is waiting on. Exactly one value per item.

values.meaning: Not yet classified; nobody has decided what it is.
Waiting on a ruling only a human may make.
Waiting on a fact or answer only a human holds.
Waiting on the accountable owner to accept the result.
Ready for an agent to produce a plan.
Ready for an agent to produce a candidate change.
A candidate exists and is waiting on review.
Waiting on another repository or system that owns the change.
Nothing is pending; the item is settled or closed.

work-item.blocker.description: Why a work item cannot move. Exactly one value per item; none means it is not blocked.

values.meaning: Not blocked.
Nobody named may settle the question that gates it.
The accountable owner is unassigned or unavailable.
What is being asked for is not bounded well enough to act on.
Another item or change has to land first.
The signal needed to confirm or refuse it does not exist yet.
A security, secrets, consent, or privacy question is unresolved.
No one is available to do the work.
A system outside this repository has to act.
The premise no longer holds and the item needs re-stating or closing.

verdict-request.kind.description: What is being asked of a human, with the dispositions that answer each kind.

values.meaning: Asks for a ruling that becomes a decision record.
Asks for a fact or answer the repository cannot supply.
Asks the accountable owner to approve a produced result.
Asks the owner for input only they hold, such as an environment or credential route.

verification.verdict.description: How well a claim is backed by a signal observed this time.

values.meaning: Confirmed against a signal observed on this run.
Asserted, but no signal was observed to back it.
Still being checked; no verdict yet.
The claim does not apply to this subject.
The check ran but could not decide. Never read as a pass.

comment.kind.description: What a comment on a work item is for. Exactly one kind per comment.

values.meaning: Confirms a request was received; carries no new material.
Asks for a fact needed to continue.
Asks for a ruling that will become a decision record.
Asks the accountable owner to accept a result.
Asks for review of a produced candidate.
Reports a change in state that a reader must act on.
Points at the signal backing a claim.
Records how this item relates to another item or record.
Records the answer given to a verdict request.
Corrects an earlier comment that was wrong.

closure.disposition.description: How much of what was originally asked for was actually delivered at closure.

values.meaning: Everything asked for was delivered.
Some of it was delivered; the remainder is named.
None of it was delivered; the reason is named.

readiness.blocker.description: Why a passive preview lane is not ready. Copied verbatim into the blocker code enum in distribution/preview-readiness.schema.json.

values.meaning: Nobody has confirmed who owns the package name.
The registry has no trusted publisher for the package.
Keyless publishing is not enabled for the lane.
Publishing a public preview is deliberately switched off.
Publishing to the latest tag would move consumers unintentionally.
The workflow that would cut the preview does not exist yet.
